name: Parametricism
summary: Buildings drawn by algorithm: continuous curved skins, smooth transitions and no repeated part. Zaha Hadid Architects and Patrik Schumacher made one flowing field of the façade, roof and floor, built with digital fabrication.

philosophy.core_thesis: A design is a system of linked parameters, so every part can differ and follow the others in a smooth gradient: one fluid field replaces the rigid, repeated element.
design_principles: Replace the rigid, repeated element with a continuous surface: roof, wall and floor fold into one another without an edge.
Drive the form by parameters: structure, daylight, flow of people and fabrication limits set the shape by script.
Differentiate the parts in a smooth gradient, so each panel, mullion and node differs a little from its neighbour.
Use a double-curved skin of panels with a typical size of 1.5 to 3m, and a hidden steel space frame under it.
Make the plan a field: paths, rooms and the landscape flow together, and the route has no sharp corner.
Design with digital tools from first sketch to fabrication, so the model is also the shop drawing.
anti_patterns: Orthogonal boxes, repeated identical bays and flat facades
Applied historical ornament or a symbolic pastiche
Sharp, unrelated shards with no continuity of surface
Random blob forms with no link to a parameter
A single repeated module over the whole skin
Visible joints and edges that break the flow of the surface

massing.form: A single flowing volume that rises from the ground plane and folds into wall and roof, with no clear division between them.
massing.proportion: Free: the shape follows the field; typical plan spans of 60 to 200m with a height of 20 to 50m.
massing.roof: The roof is part of the skin: it curves down into the walls and into the plaza without a parapet or eave.
massing.relation_to_ground: The ground plane lifts and folds to become the building; plazas and ramps are part of one surface.

structure.system: A steel space frame or a shell of glass-fibre-reinforced concrete, with a free double-curved skin carried on a hidden frame.
structure.span_and_module: Column-free spans of 40 to 90m; skin panels of 1.5 to 3m, each one different; columns are few and leaning.
structure.expression: The structure is hidden to keep the surface pure; the form itself shows the flow of forces.

materials.finish: Seamless and smooth: white, joint-free surfaces, or a glass skin with fine, even mullions.

facade.composition: One continuous double-curved surface with a gradient of panels; the glazed zones open and close along the curve.
facade.openings: Windows are cut as slits or gradient bands inside the skin; the window-to-wall ratio is 20 to 50%.
facade.solid_to_void: Variable: 50–80% opaque, changing along the surface.

light_and_space.daylight: Light enters through cuts and slits in the skin and gives soft gradients over the curved white walls.
light_and_space.spatial_sequence: A continuous flow: the plaza lifts into the entry, then a vast curved atrium with ramps and stairs and no hard threshold.
light_and_space.interior_character: White curving walls and soffits, floating stairs, long smooth ramps and indirect, even light.

ornament.attitude: Form is the ornament: the pattern comes from the algorithm and the gradient of the surface, not from applied decoration.

rules.rule: Vary every panel in a smooth gradient inside one continuous skin.
Make the route a continuous flow with no sharp corner and no hard threshold.
Fold the ground, wall and roof into one surface.
Span 40 to 90m without columns to give a vast, open interior.
Let the rhythm be a gradient, not a fixed beat: the panel size changes slowly.

emotion.target_response: Fluid futurism: the viewer feels a building in motion, without edges, from a digital age.

avoid_when: The brief asks for a low budget or a simple, buildable box.
The setting is historic and asks for a quiet, contextual infill.

modifiers.how: Break the continuous skin into colliding, angular shards and show the joints.

positive: continuous surface folding from ground to roof
smooth plaza that lifts into the building

canonical_works.architect: Zaha Hadid Architects with ADP Ingénierie

sources.title: Patrik Schumacher, The Autopoiesis of Architecture, vol. 2 (Wiley, 2012)
